name: Apathy
overview: Scripture warns against apathy as a dangerous spiritual condition that leads to stagnation and distance from God’s will. Proverbs highlights the slothful path as obstructed and thorny, contrasting with the clear way of the righteous, while Ecclesiastes exhorts believers to work wholeheartedly, recognizing the fleeting opportunity of life. Zephaniah condemns those who complacently assume God will neither bless nor judge, revealing a hardened heart. Christ’s admonition in Mark calls believers to vigilance and prayer, acknowledging the weakness of the flesh despite a willing spirit. The call in Romans to abhor evil and cling to good further underscores the necessity of active, sincere love rather than indifferent passivity. Together, these passages reveal that apathy is a spiritual peril that must be confronted through earnest devotion and obedience.
